Soil Type Detection Model

This repository contains a deep learning model developed for automated soil type classification from soil images. The model was trained on a labeled dataset of multiple soil categories and achieved 93% classification accuracy on the test dataset.

The objective of this model is to assist researchers, students, and agricultural practitioners in automatically identifying soil types using computer vision techniques.

Features
🌱 93% classification accuracy
📷 Image-based soil type prediction
🧠 Deep Learning/CNN model
⚡ Fast inference
🔬 Suitable for agriculture, precision farming, and soil analysis research
🛠 Ready for fine-tuning on custom soil datasets
About Variation

This variation contains the pretrained weights for the Soil Type Detection model along with the corresponding label encoder.

Included Files
modelwith93.pkl – Trained soil classification model
labelof93.pkl – Label encoder used during training

The model is intended for inference and can also be fine-tuned on additional soil image datasets.

instances.usage:
import pickle
import cv2
import numpy as np

# Load model
with open("modelwith93.pkl", "rb") as f:
    model = pickle.load(f)

# Load label encoder
with open("labelof93.pkl", "rb") as f:
    label_encoder = pickle.load(f)

# Load and preprocess image
image = cv2.imread("soil.jpg")
image = cv2.resize(image, (224, 224))
image = image.astype("float32") / 255.0
image = np.expand_dims(image, axis=0)

# Predict
prediction = model.predict(image)
predicted_class = np.argmax(prediction)

print(label_encoder.inverse_transform([predicted_class])[0])

# Model Summary

This LightGBM binary classifier predicts customer churn probability using demographic, behavioral, and contractual features from a 440K-row telecom-style dataset. Trained on tenure, usage frequency, support interactions, payment patterns, and subscription details, it outputs a calibrated churn risk score for proactive retention campaigns. The model is optimized for ROC-AUC to handle class imbalance typical in churn scenarios and is intended for batch scoring of active customer bases to prioritize outreach.

# Model Characteristics

- **Algorithm:** lightgbm_classifier
- **Problem type:** binary_classification
- **Target column:** Churn
- **Training samples:** 440,832
- **Features:** 11

# Data Overview

Trained on the Kaggle dataset [muhammadshahidazeem/customer-churn-dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/muhammadshahidazeem/customer-churn-dataset). No missing values present. Encode categorical features (Gender, Subscription Type, Contract Length) using LightGBM's native categorical support or one-hot encoding. Tree-based model requires no feature scaling. Inspect Total Spend and Payment Delay for extreme outliers; consider winsorization if heavy-tailed.

**Feature columns used:** Age, Gender, Tenure, Usage Frequency, Support Calls, Payment Delay, Subscription Type, Contract Length, Total Spend, Last Interaction

# Evaluation Results

Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation, compared against a naive baseline.

| | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| ROC_AUC (mean) | 1.0000 | 0.5000 |
| ROC_AUC (std) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |

Metric direction: higher is better.

LightGBM multiclass classifier for Kaggle Playground Series S6E7 (Predicting Student Health Risk; 3 classes at-risk/fit/unhealthy). Optuna-tuned (67 trials) on a fixed stratified 5-fold split.

- Objective: multiclass (num_class=3), balanced sample weights
- Early stopping on custom balanced-accuracy eval
- Numeric exact-value target encoding (fold-internal fit, leak-safe)
- Best params: lr=0.0767, num_leaves=32, min_child_samples=11, feature_fraction=0.592, lambda_l1=0.469, lambda_l2=2.06

# Data Overview

S6E7 train (690,088 rows x 14 features). Synthetic, derived from College Student Health Behavior Dataset.

# Evaluation Results

OOF balanced accuracy 0.95062 (5-fold), public LB 0.94997.

# Model Summary

This model predicts the unit price of retail items using customer demographics (gender, age), product category, purchase quantity, payment method, transaction date, and shopping mall location. Trained on 99,457 transactions from a multi-mall retail dataset, it captures nonlinear pricing patterns for revenue optimization and inventory planning. The LightGBM regressor is optimized for RMSE and handles categorical features efficiently after one-hot encoding.

# Model Characteristics

- **Algorithm:** lightgbm_regressor
- **Problem type:** regression
- **Target column:** price
- **Training samples:** 99,457
- **Features:** 33

# Data Overview

Trained on the Kaggle dataset [mehmettahiraslan/customer-shopping-dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mehmettahiraslan/customer-shopping-dataset). Parse invoice_date with pd.to_datetime and extract year, month, day, dayofweek, and cyclical sin/cos features for month and dayofweek. One-hot encode categorical columns (gender, category, payment_method, shopping_mall). No missing values present. Inspect price distribution for outliers; consider clipping extreme values if they are data errors.

**Feature columns used:** gender, age, category, quantity, payment_method, invoice_date, shopping_mall

# Evaluation Results

Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation, compared against a naive baseline.

| | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| RMSE (mean) | 5.2588 | 797.1854 |
| RMSE (std) | 0.3372 | 5.9878 |

Metric direction: lower is better.

##### **🏥 HealthInfo-AI: Multilingual Deep Learning Pipeline for Intelligent Medical Informatics**

**### 🚀 Project Overview**
HealthInfo-AI is a production-ready, full-stack artificial intelligence application engineered to democratize access to critical health diagnostics and medical information. Moving past traditional single-language constraints, HealthInfo-AI bridges language barriers by integrating an advanced Deep Learning classification engine with a seamless, multilingual user interface supporting English, Hindi, and Japanese. The application enables users to upload medical imagery or inputs and receive real-time, highly localized diagnostic reports and health informatics asynchronously.

##**🧠 Core Architecture & Technical Layout**
1. The Deep Learning Classification Engine (TensorFlow/Keras)The software infrastructure is powered by an optimized deep learning model trained for highly precise multi-class feature extraction:

> Localized Feature Extraction: Structured sequential convolutional and pooling layers configured to detect subtle abnormalities, tissue patterns, or structural visual markers within input data.

> Regularization Layering: Integrated Dropout and Batch Normalization architectures to eliminate overfitting and maintain inference stability across varying image resolutions.

>Activation Metrics: Utilizes optimized Softmax activation outputs paired with a Categorical Cross-Entropy loss framework to map probability distributions across distinct health diagnostic classes.

2. The Multilingual Cross-Lingual UI EngineThe standout technical capability of HealthInfo-AI is its localized translation routing layer built directly into the software application:

> Dynamic Language Mapping: Features a custom JavaScript-driven translation layer that instantly toggles the entire application DOM across English, Hindi, and Japanese without requiring an active server refresh or multiple page builds.

>Localized Data Payload: When an inference response is generated, the system maps the predicted classification index to a matching multilingual dictionary array, rendering complex health informatics in the user's selected native script dynamically.

3. Full-Stack Web Architecture (Flask Framework)The model is extracted from isolated development scripts and embedded into a reliable, enterprise-grade deployment stack:

> Asynchronous Web Server: A Python Flask backend acts as the central router, accepting incoming JSON and multipart image payloads via secure HTTP POST requests.

> Tensor Ingestion Pipeline: Inbound raw data arrays are streamed into computer vision pipelines, resized to exact input dimensions, normalized, and executed against the live TensorFlow model instance.

###**🛠️ Production Directory Layout**

HealthInfo-AI/
│
├── app.py                  # Central Flask core managing model routing, validation, and APIs
├── model/
│   └── health_info_model.h5 # Core TensorFlow/Keras neural network weights
│
├── templates/
│   └── index.html          # Dynamic, responsive web application UI layout
│
├── static/
│   ├── css/
│   │   └── interface.css   # Clean, modern, accessible design styling
│   └── js/
│       ├── main.js         # Fetch API handling asynchronous server communications
│       └── translate.js    # Client-side English/Hindi/Japanese language switching matrix
│
└── requirements.txt        # Production dependency log (TensorFlow, Flask, NumPy)

###**📊 Mathematical Foundations & Optimization**

The analytical foundation of HealthInfo-AI scales directly with advanced statistical learning and machine learning mathematics:

> Multivariate Vector Projections: Leveraging multidimensional spatial distributions to track decision boundaries between individual target classes.

> Gradient Backpropagation: Utilizing multi-variable calculus partial derivatives to continuously minimize the global error surface during the training loop, ensuring optimal weight convergence.

###**🔮 Future Roadmap & Deployment Goals**
The strategic roadmap for HealthInfo-AI focuses on transitioning the core code into high-impact, global environments:

> Edge-AI Clinical Integration: Compiling the full-stack Flask/TensorFlow pipeline into lightweight, low-power edge computing devices for rural clinics experiencing connectivity bottlenecks.

> MEXT Framework Strategy: Aligning the multilingual engine (specifically the Japanese language translation matrix) with global development standards, positioning it as an ideal case study for localized tech deployment inside advanced healthcare markets like Japan.

# FSOT-2.1-Instruct-0.5B

**FSOT 2.1 Instruct (0.5B)** — open instruct model derived from
[`Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct) with
**FSOT-guided pathway post-training** (isolated math / MCQ / code / ontology
LoRAs, domain-map routing during research training, anti-poison gates).

This release is a **single dense checkpoint** (pathway LoRAs weighted-merged
then `merge_and_unload`) so it loads with standard:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("PATH_OR_HUB_ID", trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("PATH_OR_HUB_ID", trust_remote_code=True)
```

Compatible with **lm-evaluation-harness**, Hugging Face model hub upload,
and Kaggle Models / notebooks.

## Method (short)

- Base: Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct
- Training: pathway-isolated LoRA (r=8) on FSOT-routed curricula
- Research system keeps adapters separate at inference (anti-poison)
- **Leaderboard export**: weighted merge of pathway adapters → merge into base
- FSOT influence: foundational seeds / domain map / D_eff routing during train;
  release is a standard causal LM

### Merge weights used for this file

```json
{
  "ontology": 0.08,
  "math": 0.25,
  "mcq": 0.35,
  "code": 0.32
}
```

Source pathway set: `C:\Users\damia\Desktop\fsot 2.1 llm\llm\models\pathway_adapters\20260717T130125Z_deepen_mcq`

### Internal refine-loop scores (n≈16, not official leaderboard)

| Pack | Accuracy |
|------|----------|
| gsm8k | 25.0% |
| arc_easy | 75.0% |
| mmlu | 68.8% |
| humaneval | 93.3% |

These are **not** lm-eval full-set numbers. Run the official harness before claiming leaderboard results.

## Intended use

- Small-model instruct / code / science QA experiments
- Baseline for FSOT routing research vs merged export
- Community leaderboard submissions (after full lm-eval)

## Limitations

- 0.5B parameter scale — not frontier SOTA overall
- Merged export can lag the multi-adapter research stack on some packs
- Math (GSM8K) remains the weakest pathway in refine loops
- Always report **full harness** numbers, not n=16 refine scores

## License

Apache-2.0 for this merge packaging and adapters contribution, subject to the
base model license (Qwen). Cite both.

## Citation

```
@software{fsot_21_instruct_05b,
  title  = {FSOT 2.1 Instruct 0.5B},
  year   = {2026},
  note   = {Derived from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct with FSOT pathway post-training}
}
```

# FSOT 2.1 Instruct 0.5B (PyTorch / Transformers)

## Load on Kaggle

`python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import torch

# Kaggle mounts the model here after you Attach the model to the notebook:
path = "/kaggle/input/fsot-21-instruct-05b/pytorch/transformers/1"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    path, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True
)
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function that adds two numbers."}]
text = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
inputs = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=128, do_sample=False)
print(tok.decode(out[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))
`

## lm-evaluation-harness (GPU notebook)

`python

`

## Notes

- Dense merge of FSOT pathway LoRAs (math/mcq/code/ontology) onto Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct
